gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-noto-sans-sc: Blockletter draws every stroke with a pencil's unchanging pressure, giving headings a precise, drafted look; Noto Sans SC follows in a plain sans with open curves. Use the heading large.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-noto-sans-sidd: Blockletter has a bulky middle and joins no thinner than its stems, so headings look sketched and exact, while Noto Sans Siddham stays friendly beneath. The two give the page a crisp top and a loose, easy text.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-noto-sans-sunu: Noto Sans Sunuwar reads openly, its curves leaving daylight and its ascender stems staying stubby. Blockletter above it is wirelike and exact, so give it the big display sizes and let the sans-serif text sit smaller.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-noto-sans-sylo: Crisp, drafted, unshaded: Blockletter draws uninterrupted monoline strokes with a bulky middle that stands out at once. Noto Sans Syloti Nagri then handles the text, its short ascenders and open-bowled a keeping things clear, with Blockletter best left big and brief.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-noto-sans-syri: Blockletter holds a flat, unvarying line weight in every letter, with a bulky middle that feels drafted and modern. Noto Sans Syriac Eastern adds a lighter, lifted text beneath it.

Blockletter's strokes never swell or thin, so each heading looks pencilled with one steady pressure and a bulky middle. Noto Sans Syriac Western supplies dense, compact text, and the pairing's sharpest quality is that precise hard edge against it.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-noto-sans-tagb: Blockletter looks cut out with a router bit, bulky in the middle. Noto Sans Tagbanwa answers with open curves and clear gaps, and the strongest quality here is how crisp and modern both feel.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-noto-sans-tai-: Blockletter has crossbars as thick as its stems and a bulky middle, so headings look drafted and exact. Noto Sans Tai Tham over many lines gives a plain sans texture, lowercase crowding the capital line.

Noto Sans Tai Viet reads crisply, with short ascenders and terminals pulled back from each curve's close. Blockletter handles the round-pen heading work, while Noto Sans Tai Viet carries the longer lines of text.
gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-noto-sans-takr: Blockletter has smooth curves with no pinching and a bulky middle, a precise, pencilled look for headings. Noto Sans Takri follows in a plain sans with generously unclosed rounds.
